content_html_sanitized:
The quality of the public discourse on cannabis prohibition in the UK is utterly wretched, to put as politely as possible.

See

The UK Can’t Even Keep Drugs Out Of Prisons But Insist They Can And Should Keep Cannabis Out Of Society. The 130 Year Decline and Fall Since The Indian Hemp Commission Report

 

A news story or editorial about cannabis usually begins with an anecdote about someone going insane after using cannabis.

See

The UK Has Some of the Highest Drug Overdose Death Rates in Europe But The New York Times Does A Major Story On “Cali Weed” Smuggled Into The UK and Misses the Real Story

And

Scotland Forever? Not With This Drugs Policy

 

Of course, they are very proud of the (apparent) decline of cannabis use, which they attribute to prohibition.

See Cannabis use decreased from 7.6% (around 2.5 million people) to 6.8% (around 2.3 million people), returning to levels seen a decade ago.

 

But…

Meanwhile, UK ranked second-worst for mental health, global survey finds

 

So, if cannabis is such a threat to mental health, how is it that one of the few countries where cannabis use has actually decreased happens to have the second worst mental health problems.
